newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU goes online in bid to crack trade barriers.
newsitem.headline: EU goes online in bid to crack trade barriers.

text.p: The European Commission has taken to the internet in a bid to break through trade barriers around the world.
The Commission on Wednesday unveiled a web site giving details of trade restrictions faced by European companies.
The site (http://mkaccdb.eu.int) gives a comprehensive country-by-country and sector-by-sector analysis of tariffs and non-tariff barriers reported to the Commission's trade department.
It also invites European companies to contribute examples of barriers they come across in order to build its market access data base.
"It is a good use of new technology to tackle an old problem," a spokesman for the commission said.

The site is easily accessible from servers based within the EU, but those connecting from outside the 15-nation bloc need a password which can be obtained from the European Commission at "market.access@dg1.cec.be".
Alternatively, the password application procedure is given when non-EU internet users attempt to connect to the site.
